newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court jails promoter over BP Tower sale.
newsitem.headline: French court jails promoter over BP Tower sale.

text.p: A French court on Friday sentenced a building developer to six months in prison for bribery in the sale of the Paris headquarters of British Petroleum in 1988.

Developer Christian Schwartz, director of Patrimoine et Investissement, one of two companies that set up French property firm Paul Doumer in order to purchase BP Tower, was given a three year sentence, of which two and a half years were suspended, plus a 500,000 franc ($86,000) fine.

The court gave Briton Clive Llewellyn and Frenchman Benoit Michelon, two executives of Feau-Hampton, a third company involved in the deal, suspended sentences of 18 months and two years respectively and fined 200,000 francs ($35,000) each.
They were found guilty of paying seven million francs ($1.2 million) in illegal commissions during the deal, apparently to enable them to buy the building for less than its full value.

Briton Paul Gatrill, who was responsible for BP's real estate until 1990, was found guilty of pocketing one million ($175,000) francs in return for giving inside information to Feau-Hampton and unduly favouring the winning bidder over rivals.
The court ordered all four men to pay three millions francs ($575,000) in damages to BP, which had sued them for the money it lost in the sale.

BP Tower, an office block in Paris's La Defense business district, was sold for 531 million francs to the Paul Doumer firm in 1988. It was sold again two years later for 1.1 billion francs ($192 million).
Fifteen other defendants were given assorted suspended sentences and fines, while a 16th suspect was cleared.
